title: Ordinary etale adjoint on strict coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and write $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $Y$ need not be separated over $k$. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For a scheme $T$, use the category $\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ of strict varying-coefficient systems and its derived category defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. On this category $j_{!,A}$ means termwise extension by zero and $p_{A,*}$ means termwise ordinary etale direct image, and put $F_{f,A}=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}$.

The functor $F_{f,A}:D(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))\to D(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ has an $O$-linear exact right adjoint $G_{f,A}$ on these unbounded derived categories of systems. For every $n$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_nG_{f,A}M\cong f_n^\times(e_nM),$$
where $f_n^\times$ is the ordinary etale right adjoint at $A_n$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The comparisons identify the evaluated units, counits and transition maps with their adjunction mates at the finite coefficient levels. There is an integer $c_f\geq0$, independent of $n$, such that $G_{f,A}$ sends $D^{\geq a}(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ into $D^{\geq a-c_f}(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))$ for every integer $a$. It sends every bounded-below normalized system to a bounded-below normalized system, with normalization as explicitly defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. These assertions are for actual functors and natural transformations in the derived category of strict coefficient systems, including their map action and independence of complex resolutions.

For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ with $O'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, use the coefficient system $B_n=O'/\varpi^nO'$ and the exact levelwise extension of scalars $T_{B/A}$ (each $B_n$ is finite free over $A_n$). The canonical scalar comparison is an isomorphism of functors of derived systems
$$T_{B/A}G_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,B}T_{B/A}.$$
Here $G_{f,B}$ is the same right-adjoint construction with $O'$ and the non-zero-divisor $\varpi$; normalization is relative to its powers. These comparisons respect the identity extension and composition, quotient maps and the canonical tensor associators. If $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $O'$ and $e$ is the ramification index, $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{en}O'$, so restriction to these levels is the cofinal subsequence of the system indexed by powers of $\varpi'$. Restricting the construction to that subsequence agrees with the construction just stated, including its maps. No inverse limit, completed integral output, constructible restriction or pro-etale exceptional adjoint is asserted in this lemma.

source.place: Constructions 5.14–5.15, Lemma 5.16 and the Brown adjoint following it (printed pp. 34–35); Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24 (printed pp. 36–37), with the bounded-below equivalence of normalization conditions in Lemma 4.13 (printed p. 24). The finite-free scalar comparison is the finite-free instance of the tensor/adjunction construction in Proposition 2.29(2) and its system version in Construction 5.15; cofinal indexing uses Construction 4.1. The bound c_f follows from the finite cohomological amplitude [0,2d] in Construction 5.15 by adjunction.

proof.text: Prepare the coefficient and site hypotheses. The valuation-ring theorem gives a DVR $O$ with finite residue field and factorization $x=u\varpi^v$. Its finite-quotient theorem gives finite rings $A_n$ and the surjective coefficient transitions. The absolute value extending that of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ has $|\ell|<1$, so a power of $\ell$ lies in $(\varpi^n)$; thus each $A_n$ is annihilated by an integer invertible on $k$. Completeness of $E$ makes its closed valuation subring complete: a $\varpi$-adic Cauchy sequence is Cauchy in $E$ and its limit still has absolute value at most one. Hence $O=\varprojlim O/\varpi^n$. Finite-type schemes over $k$, including $\overline X$, are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem (a field is Noetherian). The system comparison theorem therefore supplies the unbounded derived direct image and its evaluated comparisons. Extension by zero for $j$ is exact and left adjoint to restriction; its termwise version acts on strict systems and on the enhanced section models. Consequently $F=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}$ is a well-defined exact functor, and $e_nF\cong F_{f,A_n}e_n$, with actual units, counits, and coefficient transition maps. The left-extension lemma supplies Grothendieckness, levelwise coproducts and detection by evaluation.

First construct the coefficient projection square at an ordinary finite level. For any homomorphism of finite $\ell$-primary rings $C\to D$, let $T=-\otimes_C^LD$ and let $U$ be exact restriction of scalars. The module tensor/restriction adjunction derives to $T\dashv U$: restriction is exact and derived tensor is computed by K-flat resolutions. Composition for unbounded derived direct images, applied to the square of identity-topos ring-change morphisms and the geometric proper map, gives $URp_{*,D}\cong Rp_{*,C}U$. It also gives $UF_{f,D}\cong F_{f,C}U$, since extension by zero commutes with restriction. Form the $D$-linear map $q:T_YF_{f,C}\to F_{f,D}T_X$ by tensor/restriction adjunction from $F_{f,C}$ applied to the scalar unit. After forgetting $D$, this is exactly the constant-coefficient projection map for $V=D$, hence is invertible by the finite-level tensor lemma (equivalently use the proper projection formula and the exact open extension). Restriction detects isomorphisms, so $q$ is invertible as a $D$-linear map. This argument applies to non-flat quotient maps as well as finite-free extensions. On the enhanced section models the same counit-transpose construction supplies an actual map, not a choice of componentwise lifts. Evaluation of that map is the map just constructed. Its identity and composite-extension squares agree: on K-flat representatives the scalar units send $x$ to $x\otimes1$, and the associator sends $(x\otimes d)\otimes d'$ to $x\otimes dd'$; these give the same transpose for either composite.

The preceding squares, with $C=A_n,D=A_m$ for $m\le n$, give $FL_n\cong L_nF_{f,A_n}$: at $m\le n$ it is precisely $q$, and at $m>n$ both evaluations are zero. The section-model construction and the transition formulas for $L_n$ identify the maps and their coherences, so this is an isomorphism of functors on derived systems. Also $F$ preserves arbitrary set-indexed coproducts. Indeed $j_!$ preserves them as a left adjoint, proper $Rp_*$ preserves them for each finite ring by the proper-coproduct theorem, and evaluation computes coproducts and detects isomorphisms. Apply the Grothendieck-derived Brown theorem to this exact coproduct-preserving functor, obtaining an actual right adjoint $G$. Its additive and $O$-linear structure is specified by the adjunction: the map induced by $a\in O$ is the unique transpose of multiplication by $a$ on $F$; the identities for sums and products follow from the Hom bijection. Similarly $G(M[t])\cong(GM)[t]$ is the unique adjunction-induced shift isomorphism. The shift cocycle and compatibility of the unit and counit follow by transposition from those for $F$. The triangulated-right-adjoint lemma then proves $G$ exact.

source.place: Lemma 5.16 and the Brown right adjoint following it.

proof.text:
For $P\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ and $M\in D(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$, use the following natural Hom bijections:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_nGM)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_nP,GM)=\operatorname{Hom}(FL_nP,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_nF_{f,A_n}P,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,A_n}P,e_nM)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,f_n^\times e_nM).$$
Taking the images of identity morphisms in the two directions produces inverse natural maps $e_nG\cong f_n^\times e_n$; their inverse equations follow immediately by composing the displayed bijections. This is the Yoneda argument written out, not an appeal to full faithfulness of a representable embedding. The adjunction formulas define the comparison to preserve the evaluated counits and units. For $m\ge n$, the structure map is the mate of the transition together with the coefficient square $q$ of step 2: its adjoint transition is the scalar comparison $T_{A_n/A_m}f_m^\times(M_m)\to f_n^\times(T_{A_n/A_m}M_m)$ followed by $f_n^\times$ of the adjoint input transition. This equation follows by transposing both maps, which yields the input transition composed with the same evaluated counit and $q^{-1}$. It therefore identifies transitions as maps, including composition for three indices.

source.place: Lemma 5.22, including its proof by the two adjunctions in Lemma 5.16.

proof.text:
Choose the uniform integer $N_f$ from the finite-level amplitude lemma. If $H\in D^{\le b}(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))$, its evaluations satisfy the same bound; therefore $FH\in D^{\le b+N_f}$ by that lemma and evaluation detection. If $M\in D^{\ge a}$ and $H\in D^{\le a-N_f-1}$, then
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,GM)=\operatorname{Hom}(FH,M)=0.$$
The orthogonality characterization of the standard cohomological truncations gives $GM\in D^{\ge a-N_f}$. To spell out the characterization used here, take $H=\tau_{\le a-N_f-1}GM$; its canonical map to $GM$ must vanish, whereas it induces the identity on all cohomology in those degrees, so those groups vanish. Thus $c_f=N_f$ works independently of the level.

source.place: Construction 5.15, amplitude [0,2d], and its right adjoint after Lemma 5.16.

proof.text:
Show that the finite-level right adjoints commute with every constant finite change of coefficients, including non-flat quotients. With $T,U,q$ as in step 2, adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,UG_{f,D}N)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_XK,G_{f,D}N)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,D}T_XK,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_YF_{f,C}K,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,G_{f,C}U N).$$
Identity morphisms again give $UG_{f,D}\cong G_{f,C}U$. Define $b:T_XG_{f,C}M\to G_{f,D}T_YM$ as the transpose of
$$F_{f,D}T_XG_{f,C}M\xrightarrow{q^{-1}}T_YF_{f,C}G_{f,C}M\xrightarrow{T_Y\epsilon_C}T_YM.$$
Under the preceding restriction identification, $Ub$ is exactly $D\otimes_C^LG_{f,C}M\to G_{f,C}(D\otimes_C^LM)$, the constant-tensor map of the finite-level lemma with $V=D$. That lemma makes it invertible; exact restriction is conservative, hence $b$ is invertible. For a normalized system $M$, step 4 identifies its output's adjoint transition as
$$A_n\otimes^L_{A_m}G_{f,A_m}M_m\xrightarrow{b}G_{f,A_n}(A_n\otimes^L_{A_m}M_m)\xrightarrow{G_{f,A_n}(\alpha_{m,n})}G_{f,A_n}M_n.$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms. Thus $GM$ is normalized, and step 5 supplies boundedness below when $M$ is bounded below. This uses only the explicitly stated derived-transition definition of normalization; no unbounded equivalence with completion is presumed.

source.place: Proposition 2.29(2); Lemma 5.22 and its observation on weak normalization; Proposition 5.24. The normalization convention is the transition condition of the item.

proof.text: For the arithmetic coefficient input, identify O prime with the integral closure of O in E prime using lem-sfb-padic-integers-integral-closure. The DVR theorem supplies the fraction field E and the PID structure on O. E prime is finite over E by restriction of scalars and separable because E has characteristic zero. The finite-integral-closure theorem therefore gives a finite O-module O prime, and IsIntegralClosure.module_free gives freeness over the PID O. Take its finite basis, base change it to O/(varpi^(n+1)), and use Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor. Ideal.map_pow and Ideal.map_span identify the extended ideal with the ideal generated by the image uniformizer power. Transport the resulting basis to the actual ModuleCat.restrictScalars quotient module, with its scalar action explicitly Module.compHom of strictCoefficientRingMap. This proves strictEtaleScalarLevelModule_finiteFree without a completeness or residue-quotient argument. Separately, strictEtaleIntegerMap_mem follows by identifying the spectral norms under an injective algebra map using minpoly.algHom_eq, then applying the unit-ball descriptions from the DVR theorem. The remaining ramification and cofinal-construction assertions are still the unproved plan of step 9.

source.place: Construction 4.1, allowing any principal non-zero-divisor with complete adic topology; coefficient change used in Proposition 2.29(2).

proof.text: On derived systems let $U$ be exact restriction of scalars for $B_\bullet/A_\bullet$. Tensor/restriction adjunction derives to $T\dashv U$, with evaluations and units computed termwise; here finite freeness also makes $T$ exact. The enhanced section models supply the actual projection square $q:T_YF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_X$ constructed in step 2; its evaluations are those finite-level isomorphisms, so it is invertible. Define the actual system transformation $b:T_XG_A\to G_BT_Y$ by the identical transpose formula $T\epsilon_A\circ q^{-1}$ used in step 6. Step 4 and the compatibility of transposition with the specified section models identify its evaluations with the finite-level $b$ of step 6. They are all invertible, so $b$ is an isomorphism of derived-system functors. For an identity coefficient extension its transpose is the counit and $b$ is the identity. For two extensions, transpose the composite of their $b$ maps and use the defining equations $\epsilon_D\circ F_Db=T\epsilon_C\circ q^{-1}$ twice. Naturality of the counits reduces the result to $T'T\epsilon_C$ preceded by the composite inverse projection square. The associativity equation for $q$ in step 2 identifies this with the transpose defining $b$ for the composite extension. The Hom bijection is injective, so the two actual system maps agree. This argument also applies to diagrams containing quotient maps, using derived tensor for their non-flat edges. It proves the requested coherences with identities, composition, quotients and the canonical tensor associators; it does not use faithfulness of evaluation on morphisms.

Finally consider any strictly increasing unbounded subsequence $r$. Its restriction $U_r$ has left adjoint $L_r$ by the left-extension lemma. The explicit formula for $L_r$ and the coefficient projection squares of step 2 give $F_{\mathrm{full}}L_r\cong L_rF_r$ as actual functors: at level $m$ use $q$ for $B_{r(t(m))}\to B_m$; the transition formulas and the scalar-unit calculation in step 2 give the required compatible maps. For any $N$ in the subsequence source category and $M$ in the full target category, the bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,U_rG_{\mathrm{full}}M)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_rN,G_{\mathrm{full}}M)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\mathrm{full}}L_rN,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_rF_rN,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_rU_rM)$$
give the canonical counit-preserving isomorphism $U_rG_{\mathrm{full}}\cong G_rU_r$. It is natural on maps and coherent under composed subsequences by composition of these Hom bijections, or equivalently by equality of their counit transposes. Apply it to the $O'$ tower indexed by $\varpi'$ and $r(n)=en$. The coefficient ideals identified in step 7 identify its restricted ring system with $B_n=O'/\varpi^nO'$, so this is exactly the required comparison with the construction using $\varpi$. Every comparison above was defined by derived operations and an adjunction transpose, which are independent of resolutions by the change-of-rings, system comparison and enhanced-model lemmas; no inverse limit or integral output was introduced.

split_report.summary: Unchanged statement. Constructed the ambient system right adjoint by Brown, evaluated it with derived left extensions, derived the uniform lower bound by truncation orthogonality, and proved normalization using constant-coefficient tensor rather than flatness of quotient rings. Two new prerequisites: generic derived left-extension calculus for semilinear systems and finite-level constant-tensor/amplitude calculus. Actual coefficient and subsequence maps are defined by counit transposition; coherence is proved before evaluation. No Lean was written or compiled.
